topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture opens with an introduction to the speaker, course outline, and the core learning outcomes on cancer causes.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Etiology and Environmental Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of cancer etiology by examining the interaction between intrinsic cellular errors, environmental mutagens, and population-level epidemiology.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how infectious pathogens drive cancer development, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Direct Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how chemical and physical agents cause direct DNA damage and bulky adducts following host metabolic activation.

topics.label: Cancer Initiation and Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic carcinogenesis by differentiating tumor initiators from promoters that drive cellular proliferation and chronic inflammation.

topics.label: Host Developmental Susceptibility and Mechanistic Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how host developmental timing influences cancer susceptibility and provide a consolidated summary of carcinogenic pathways.

topics.label: Methodologies for Demonstrating Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, experimental, and epidemiological methods used to demonstrate carcinogenicity and weigh health risks.
